consensus_findings.description: Critical: skills/tests/supervise/test_digest_schemas.py:15 pins openspec/changes/add-supervisor-candidate-work-digest/contracts/schemas as a literal path. skills/tests/openspec_paths/test_change_path_stability.py already fails on this file, and archival will move the directory so the byte-identity check breaks on landing day rather than contract drift.

Nit: test_supervisor_record_schema.py mutates approved digested_stubs in memory (rewriting stub_key/suggested_change_id and injecting route/roadmap_ref) before validating full.json, mirror.json, and handoff-with-record.json. Those on-disk fixtures no longer satisfy the tightened schemas, so the tests no longer prove the checked-in fixtures are valid.

Optional: task 0.1 / spec scenario 'Score coverage must exactly match each batch' calls out scores outside 1–5, and the rubric schema correctly rejects them, but test_digest_schemas.py has no explicit out-of-range score assertion (only missing factor/justification and key-coverage cases).

FYI: cycle_state._clean_digested_stub still accepts the pre-contract stub_key pattern ^(change|prov):.+$ and still drops roadmap_ref/route/until/reason. Approved records that pass the new schemas would be stripped back to the old shape if cleaned by today's sanitizer. Design D5 assigns that update to later digest-module work, not wp-contracts.

none: Approved/rejected decision conditions match the Digest Approval Routing requirement: approved requires non-null route; refine-roadmap requires a roadmap_ref string; plan-roadmap requires roadmap_ref const null; rejected requires reason; deferred permits optional until. Full and mirror digestedStub definitions are identical, and supervisor-decisions fixtures round-trip both schemas.

none: Package scope is clean — every files_modified path is inside write_allow, deny is untouched, locks match the declared contract set, and change-local rubric/digest schemas are byte-identical to the durable openspec/schemas/supervise-*.schema.json installs so runtime lookup does not depend on the active change directory.

none: Contracts stay data-only — additionalProperties is false on digest/rubric/ranked objects, stub_key and suggested_change_id patterns reject path-like and non-canonical keys, and untrusted provenance read/redaction policy is correctly left to digest.py rather than encoded as false safety in the schema.

none: RubricScore.scores carries minItems 1 and maxItems 20, matching the bounded batch size from the Candidate-Work Digest requirement and preventing schema-valid oversized score documents from entering rank.

none: test_score_coverage_semantics_reject_duplicate_missing_and_unknown_keys pins the application-level rank defects (duplicate=/missing=/unknown=) that JSON Schema cannot express, so later digest.py work inherits an explicit, named failure contract rather than an informal comment.

none: Digest weights are frozen as consts (including risk_higher_is_safer, bucket orders, staleness penalty/cap, and stub_key:asc tie-break), so a ranked digest cannot silently reinterpret scores under a drifted policy document; invalid or partial score docs remain schema-invalid before any cache/digest write owned by later packages.
Newly added JSON schemas for digest and rubric-score correctly define the contract for supervisor candidate work digest functionality.
Extended supervisor-record schemas correctly add decision metadata fields (roadmap_ref, route, until, reason) with proper conditional validation constraints.
Schema validation tests comprehensively cover positive cases, negative validation scenarios, and edge cases for stub key formats and decision metadata combinations.
Changes properly separate concerns between runtime schemas (in openspec/schemas/) and local change schemas (in openspec/changes/add-supervisor-candidate-work-digest/contracts/schemas/).
Schema definitions appropriately constrain input data with regex patterns, enum values, and required field validations to prevent injection or malformed data issues.
Schema design follows efficient JSON structure patterns with appropriate typing and constraints for parsing performance.
Schema files follow consistent JSON formatting and documentation conventions with clear field descriptions.
Schema definitions include sufficient metadata fields (fingerprint, timestamps, weights) to enable tracking and debugging of digest generation processes.
Schema design includes appropriate nullable fields and error handling patterns to support graceful degradation scenarios.
Schema changes maintain backward compatibility through additive changes and proper versioning (schema_version: 1).
